title: ADR-0040 — Multi-Runtime Selection Matrix Rules
description: Machine-readable rules encoding ADR-0040 Multi-Runtime Selection. Defines runtime selection by workload profile and inter-runtime communication rules.

rules.title: Runtime selected by workload profile only
rules.description: Teams MUST select the target runtime based exclusively on the specific workload profile. Language selection must not be based on subjective preference.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Decision: Optimized cost/performance. Each workload runs on the engine most efficient for its memory/CPU profile.
rules.validationQuery: Runtime selection documented in evolith.yaml and justified by workload profile analysis.

rules.title: Web APIs and BFF use Node.js/TypeScript
rules.description: MANDATE: Node.js/TypeScript for Web APIs, BFF, and I/O-bound workloads. Rationale: High I/O concurrency, rapid delivery, extensive community ecosystem.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Runtime Selection Matrix: Web APIs, BFF, I/O Bound → Node.js/TypeScript.
rules.validationQuery: Web API and BFF services run on Node.js. No .NET or other runtimes for these workloads without explicit ADR exception.

rules.title: High compute and batch use .NET (C#)
rules.description: MANDATE: .NET (C#) for High Compute, ETL, and Batch workloads. Rationale: Superior multi-threading performance, typed raw compute, heavy math.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Runtime Selection Matrix: High Compute, ETL, Batch → .NET (C#).
rules.validationQuery: High compute services (ETL, batch processing, mathematical computation) run on .NET. Documented workload classification in evolith.yaml.

rules.title: Mobile with hardware access uses Android/Kotlin
rules.description: MANDATE: Android (Kotlin) for Operative Mobility workloads with direct hardware peripheral access (Scanners, GPS, Cameras) and strict offline mode requirements.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Runtime Selection Matrix: Operative Mobility → Android (Kotlin).
rules.validationQuery: Mobile apps requiring hardware access run on Android/Kotlin. iOS considered only with Architecture Board exception.

rules.title: Direct runtime dependency forbidden
rules.description: Direct runtime dependency is forbidden. Communication between disparate runtimes MUST traverse explicitly defined boundaries. No Node.js code directly importing .NET assemblies or vice versa.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Decision: Runtime isolation prevents tight coupling that prevents independent evolution.
rules.validationQuery: No direct cross-runtime imports. All inter-runtime calls go through protocol boundaries (gRPC/REST).

rules.title: Synchronous inter-op uses gRPC
rules.description: Synchronous Inter-Op between runtimes (Node.js ↔ .NET) MUST mandatorily utilize gRPC (Protocol Buffers) for low-latency type-safe transmission.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Inter-Runtime Communications Rule: gRPC for synchronous inter-op.
rules.validationQuery: Node.js ↔ .NET synchronous calls use gRPC. Contract tests validate proto compatibility.

rules.title: Asynchronous inter-op uses message broker
rules.description: Asynchronous Inter-Op utilizes RabbitMQ/Kafka with contract validation via JSON-Schema or Protobuf. Contracts must be centrally stored and versioned.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Inter-Runtime Communications Rule: RabbitMQ/Kafka for async inter-op with schema validation.
rules.validationQuery: Async events validated against schema. Message broker contracts centralized in shared library.

rules.title: Contracts centrally stored and versioned
rules.description: All inter-runtime contracts must be centrally stored and versioned using semantic versioning. Changes require Pact JS/Net backward compatibility verification.
rules.rationale: ADR-0040 §Contract Registry: Centralized versioning prevents contract drift.
rules.validationQuery: Contract registry exists and is referenced by all inter-runtime communicating services.

runtimeMatrix.rationale: Direct hardware access, strict offline mode

exitCriteria.description: Runtime selection documented per service. Inter-runtime communication uses gRPC/RabbitMQ. Contracts versioned centrally.
